History:
• 25-year-old woman reports worsening anxiety for ~2 months, coinciding with starting a new, stressful head-office job in fashion retail.  
• Morning dread of leaving the house/work; feels “really nervous” daily.  
• Sleep disturbance: goes to bed 22:00-23:00, lies awake “for hours,” shallow sleep estimated 3–4 h/night; wakes early with racing heart.  
• Palpitations: irregular rapid heartbeat, usually on waking or when worried about being late; episodes last 2–10 min; denies classic chest pain but describes discomfort when heart is racing.  
• Day-time effects: marked fatigue, low energy, loss of enjoyment in hobbies (running, tennis) and socialising; still attends work but contemplates calling in sick.  
• Mood: persistently “down,” but no suicidal ideation or prior depressive episodes.  
• Triggers: work stress (unsupportive boss), crowded public transport (tube).  
• Appetite largely unchanged except increased chocolate intake.  
• Alcohol: binge-drinks most Fridays/Saturdays (“over my limit”) plus occasional weekday glass of wine.  
• Tobacco: occasional smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: none.  
• Lives with parents; mother has history of depression.  
• No prior counselling; mother advised GP review.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses, surgeries, or prior mental-health diagnoses documented.  
• Allergies: not documented (missing).  
• Current medications: none reported (medication list missing).  

Physical Examination:
• Tele-consultation; no formal exam performed.  
• Patient appeared distressed/anxious on video.  
• Reports episodic palpitations; no reported syncope.  
• No acute chest pain, throat swelling, or breathing difficulty noted.

Impression:
• Work-related generalized anxiety with insomnia and stress-related palpitations (likely anxiety-mediated).

Management Plan:
• Provide self-referral link to NHS talking therapies (CBT-based).  
• Share online anxiety-management and sleep-hygiene resources.  
• Order basic blood tests (e.g., FBC, TFTs, electrolytes) to exclude metabolic causes of palpitations; patient to phone support line to arrange phlebotomy.  
• Schedule GP follow-up ~1 week after labs to review results and clinical progress.  
• Advise patient to seek earlier review if anxiety escalates, daily function deteriorates, or palpitations worsen.  
• Discussed that medication (e.g., SSRIs) may be considered later if non-pharmacological measures insufficient.

Patient Summary:
Ms Valerie Cole presents with a two-month history of escalating job-related anxiety, insomnia, and episodic palpitations. Clinical picture suggests generalized anxiety disorder without suicidal risk. She was directed to CBT resources and basic labs have been arranged; follow-up planned in one week.

Key Takeaways:
• Self-refer to talking therapy using the provided NHS link.  
• Begin online anxiety and sleep-hygiene exercises immediately.  
• Arrange ordered blood tests and attend follow-up to review results.

Next Steps:
• Complete blood tests (FBC, TFTs, U&E) as soon as possible.  
• GP review 1 week post-testing.  
• Continue monitoring mood/sleep; return sooner if symptoms intensify or interfere with work/ADLs.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: allergies, current medication list, full past medical history, vital signs, physical examination.  
• Internal conflicts: patient initially denies chest pain but later says heart beating fast is “painful” (minor conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: clear audio; minimal background noise; suitable for documentation.
